answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a canyon for malicious actors, rendering the cost of deploying infinite Sybil identities prohibitively expensive through capital lockups. By requiring validators to stake tokens to secure the network, the protocol turns the vast horizon of potential fake identities into an economic oasis for honest participants. An attacker must acquire a majority of the circulating supply to subvert consensus, forcing the cost of the attack to scale linearly with the total value secured by the network.
